Management cites strong growth in China but gives no figure.
cucinelli.watch: Check whether the company publishes regional figures for the quarter and puts a growth number on China and Asia, and how growth compares with the 11.9% the group must lap next quarter.

ferragamo.note: Ferragamo's Q3 2026 growth at Constant FX was -3.5%, down from 4.6% in Q2 2026, a change of -8.1 points. Asia Pacific was the main drag, at -11.1% after a 0.6% decline in the prior quarter. North America was the only region that grew, at 2.4%. Japan was -5.0% and EMEA was -5.2%. Growth was 7.7 points behind the median of the other personal luxury goods companies, at 4.2%.
ferragamo.watch: Check whether Asia Pacific, and China in particular, stops deteriorating and whether growth broadens beyond North America against the easier base of -2.0% in the year-earlier quarter.

pandora.note: Pandora's organic growth was 6% in Q3 2026, up from 3% in Q2 2026, a change of 3 points. That is ahead of the median of the other personal luxury goods companies at 2.5%, a gap of 3.5 points. Management said Asia-Pacific like-for-like sales grew 20%, led by Japan. Guidance was narrowed to organic growth of 2% to 3% in 2026 from 0% to 3%, with an EBIT margin of 22.5% to 23%.
pandora.watch: Check whether organic growth holds against the 4% growth it laps next quarter and whether Asia-Pacific like-for-like sales stay led by Japan.

ferrari.note: Ferrari's Q3 2026 growth at Constant FX was 10%, down from 11% in Q2 2026, a slowdown of 1 point. Cars and spare parts grew 10%, Sponsorship, commercial and brand grew 7%, and Other grew 17%. The two-year stack is 20.2%. Ferrari shipped 3,368 cars, 33 fewer than a year earlier. Guidance is about €7.65 billion in 2026, raised from about €7.60 billion.
ferrari.watch: Check whether growth in cars and spare parts holds against the easier base of 6% to be lapped next quarter, and whether shipments rise or fall against the year earlier.

aston-martin.note: Aston Martin's reported revenue growth was 36% in Q3 2026, against 62% in Q2 2026, a slowdown of 26 points. The company gives no revenue by region or segment, so the change cannot be traced to a market. The scope note says Valhalla deliveries make revenue swing from quarter to quarter. Growth a year earlier was -27%, and the rate to lap next quarter is -12%. Full-year 2026 guidance is unchanged.
aston-martin.watch: Check whether reported revenue growth holds up against the tougher base of -12% and whether Valhalla deliveries again drive the quarterly swing.

ralph-lauren.note: Ralph Lauren's constant FX growth was 10% in Q3 2026, down from 13% in Q2 2026, a change of -3 points. North America was the main driver, with its contribution down 7 points, and it grew 6%. Europe grew 3%. Asia (incl. Japan) grew 28%, up 3 points. All 3 reported regions grew. Growth was 6.5 points ahead of the median of the other accessible luxury companies at 3.5%.
ralph-lauren.watch: Check whether North America growth steadies against the 10% group growth that is to be lapped next quarter, and whether Asia (incl. Japan) holds its pace.

tapestry.note: Tapestry's constant FX growth was 12% in Q3 2026, up from 11% in Q2 2026, a gain of 1 point. Greater China drove the change, growing 39%, 11 points faster than the prior quarter. Europe grew 22%, while North America and Japan each grew 4%. Coach grew 16% and Kate Spade was -10%. Growth was 9.4 points above the median of the other accessible luxury companies at 2.5%. All 4 reported regions grew.
tapestry.watch: Check whether Greater China growth holds up against the 18% group growth the company must lap next quarter, and whether Kate Spade improves from -10%.

capri.note: Capri Holdings' constant FX growth was -4.9% in Q3 2026, against -4.1% in Q2 2026, a change of -0.8 points. The two-year stack was -8.9%. Michael Kors fell 8.0% while Jimmy Choo grew 12.2%. The company was 15.9 points behind the median of the other accessible luxury companies, which grew 11.0%. Capri gives no regional growth, and no figure for China.
capri.watch: Check whether Michael Kors growth improves from -8.0% and whether Jimmy Choo keeps growing against the comparison of -5.9% for the whole company.
